confidence_notes: I ran three web searches: the RBA rate and two for Melbourne prices. The price searches returned secondary cost-of-living aggregators, not the Numbeo page itself, and their dates and quality vary. Restaurant and coffee anchors are fairly well supported: cappuccino about A$5-5.50, inexpensive meal about A$20-25, and mid-range meal for two about A$120-150. Beer is supported by sources giving A$11-15 for a local pint, and I took a standard serving at the lower-middle of that range. Wine is based on bar prices of about A$10-15 a glass. Cocktails had no direct source, so I set them at roughly twice the beer price, in line with the A$12-25 spirits range found. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. They are the least certain anchors, because Melbourne hotel rates vary a lot with events and season.
comparable_city_reasoning: Melbourne is a large, high-cost Australian city. Anchors are based on typical Australian big-city pricing, close to Sydney, with high alcohol taxes pushing drink prices up. Restaurant prices are near the national average.
